windows.notes:
Fixes for encrypted backups. Updating is recommended.
- An encrypted copy of a damaged file no longer encrypts two different contents the same way at the same place in the file, which could reveal part of the recovered data. Copies carried on from earlier versions are encrypted again where needed.
- Backups protected with a key pair are now signed: a restore or check refuses a set that was changed by someone without your key. A job starts signing after you unlock it once with its password; older sets restore with an "unsigned" warning.
- A restore never writes through a link it restored earlier in the same run.

macos.notes:
Fixes for disk images.
- An image of a disk that was interrupted now carries on where it stopped, instead of reading the whole disk again (which wears a failing disk). It first checks a few sectors, so another disk at the same place, or an image damaged since, is imaged again.
- An image that can't be opened is never carried on in a new, empty file.
- Image a disk: the snapshot option now says that free space isn't read.
